Resumen de lo acordado, para confirmar antes de redactar el objetivo:
• El vendedor dueño de una publicación, o un admin, puede pausarla con POST /listings/:id/pause y reanudarla con POST /listings/:id/resume. Pausada tiene status paused; reanudada vuelve a active.

• Otros usuarios (otro vendedor, comprador), sin usuario o publicación inexistente: se rechaza; los códigos de error y cuerpos de respuesta exactos quedan a criterio del implementador.
• Los pedidos que ya existían quedan como están.
• Las dos rutas nuevas se publican también en la tabla de rutas del servidor real (hoy el servidor responde 404 a cualquier ruta que no esté en esa lista).
• Fuera de alcance: pausas programadas o con vencimiento, historial de pausas, notificaciones, cambios a pedidos existentes.
• No hay condiciones para detener el trabajo antes de tiempo.
Mi clasificación del tamaño (corrígela si no estás de acuerdo): estándar — agrega un estado nuevo y rutas nuevas que tocan búsqueda y pedidos; eso permite hasta 3 rondas de revisión.

questions.question:
Este es el borrador completo del objetivo (goal.md), tal cual quedaría. El trabajo termina cuando se cumple su condición y cada criterio AC está demostrado:

# Goal — Pause and resume a listing (pause-listing)

## Goal condition
`npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` exit 0, and against the real server (`npm start`, which serves the published route table): after the owning seller calls `POST /listings/:id/pause`, `GET /listings/:id` returns the listing with `status: "paused"` and an unchanged `rankScore`, `GET /listings` no longer includes it, and an order on it is rejected; after `POST /listings/:id/resume`, `GET /listings/:id` returns `status: "active"` with the same `rankScore` and `GET /listings` includes it again in its rank position.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 The owning seller of a listing can pause it with `POST /listings/:id/pause`; afterwards the listing has status `paused`.
- AC-2 The owning seller can resume a paused listing with `POST /listings/:id/resume`; afterwards the listing has status `active`.
- AC-3 An admin can pause and resume any listing, with the same effect as AC-1 and AC-2.
- AC-4 Pausing and resuming do not change the listing's `rankScore`; once resumed, the listing appears in `GET /listings` in the same position its `rankScore` gives it, as if it had never been paused.
- AC-5 While paused, the listing does not appear in `GET /listings` results for anyone, its owner included.
- AC-6 While paused, `GET /listings/:id` still returns the listing to anyone, showing status `paused`.
- AC-7 While paused, `POST /listings/:id/orders` is rejected with an error response, no order is created and the listing's `rankScore` does not change.
- AC-8 Pausing an already paused listing, or resuming an already active one, answers success and leaves the listing unchanged.
- AC-9 Pause and resume are rejected with an error response, and the listing is left unchanged, when: there is no identified user; the caller is a seller who does not own the listing; the caller is a buyer; the listing does not exist. (exact codes and bodies left to the implementer)
- AC-10 Orders that existed before the pause stay exactly as they were, and remain visible in `GET /orders` as today.
- AC-11 Both new routes are reachable on the real server: they are added to the published route table that the server puts in front of the app.

## Constraints
- Existing behavior of `GET /listings`, `GET /listings/:id`, `POST /listings`, `POST /listings/:id/orders` and `GET /orders` for active listings does not change; existing tests keep passing unchanged.
- The exact error codes and response bodies of the new routes, and of the rejected order, are the implementer's choice.
- Follow the style of the existing endpoints.

## Stop when
none

## Out of scope
- Scheduled or expiring pauses; pause history; notifications.
- Any change to existing orders (cancelling or otherwise).
- Showing paused listings in search to their owner or admins (search excludes them for everyone).

## Surfaces
- In scope: the two new routes; the published route table (`src/gateway.ts`); `GET /listings` (exclude paused); `GET /listings/:id` (shows paused); `POST /listings/:id/orders` (reject paused).
- Unchanged: `POST /listings`, `GET /orders` (existing orders untouched).

## Literals
- `POST /listings/:id/pause` / `POST /listings/:id/resume` / status `paused`

## References
None — follow the existing endpoints in `src/listings.ts` and `src/orders.ts`.

(En el archivo cada criterio lleva además una etiqueta de qué respuesta tuya lo origina.)

answers.Este es el borrador completo del objetiv: Editar: AC-4 contradice lo que necesito que quede claro. La TRUTH dice que el `rankScore` se preserva exactamente, pero que la posición de búsqueda no está garantizada — otros listings pueden haberlo adelantado mientras estaba pausado. AC-4 dice "in the same position its `rankScore` gives it, as if it had never been paused", lo que implica que regresa a su posición anterior, que no es correcto. Debe corregirse para reflejar que el ranking se recalcula después de la pausa, y otros listings pueden haberlo adelantado.

questions.question:
Corregí el criterio del ranking y la condición del objetivo; el resto del borrador queda igual que antes. Las dos partes cambiadas, tal cual quedan:

Goal condition (final): "...after `POST /listings/:id/resume`, `GET /listings/:id` returns `status: "active"` with the same `rankScore` and `GET /listings` includes it again, ordered by its preserved `rankScore` against the other listings' current scores."

AC-4: "Pausing and resuming preserve the listing's `rankScore` exactly. Its search position is not guaranteed: once resumed, `GET /listings` places it by that preserved `rankScore` against the other listings' current scores, so listings that overtook it while it was paused stay ahead of it."
